hints: A trailing zero comes from a factor 10, which needs one factor 2 and one factor 5.
Factorials contain more 2s than 5s, so count only how many factors of 5 occur in n!.
Numbers divisible by 25, 125, and higher powers contribute extra factors.
analogy: Count how many complete 2-and-5 pairs are in the factorial; the 5s are the scarce ingredient.
example: For 20!, multiples of 5 contribute four factors of 5 (5,10,15,20), so there are 4 trailing zeros.
algorithm: Add floor(n/5)+floor(n/25)+floor(n/125)+... until the power exceeds n.
correctness: Each counted factor of 5 pairs with a factor of 2 to make a decimal zero; higher powers supply additional 5s.
complexity: O(log_5 n) time and O(1) extra space.
